Beat the eggs with crushed garlic, parsley and salt and soak the steaks in it for fifteen minutes.
Press each steak firmly into breadcrumbs on both sides and shallow fry in hot oil until crisp and golden.
Lay the milanesas on a tray, spoon tomato sauce over each, add a slice of ham and cover with mozzarella.
Grill until the cheese melts and blisters, dust with oregano and serve with fries or a green salad.

recipes.name: Moros y Cristianos
steps: Soak the black beans overnight, then boil them with bay leaves until tender, keeping the inky cooking liquid.
Make a sofrito by frying chopped onion, green pepper and garlic in olive oil with cumin and oregano until soft.
Stir half the sofrito into the beans and mash a ladleful against the pot so the liquid thickens.
Add the rinsed rice and enough bean liquid to cover by a thumb, bring to a boil then drop to the lowest heat.
Cover and steam eighteen minutes, rest ten, then fork through with the remaining sofrito and a splash of oil.

recipes.name: Ital Stew
steps: Warm the coconut milk with bruised spring onion, thyme, pimento and the whole scotch bonnet, keeping the chilli unbroken for aroma without fire.
Add the cubed pumpkin and sweet potato and simmer fifteen minutes until they begin to soften and thicken the liquid.
Stir in the kidney beans and let everything bubble gently so the stew turns creamy on its own.
Fold in the chopped callaloo for the last five minutes and season with salt and black pepper.
Fish out the chilli and thyme stalks and serve with boiled dumplings or rice.

recipes.name: Escovitch Fish
steps: Score the cleaned fish to the bone, season inside and out with salt, pepper and a little garlic, and rest thirty minutes.
Fry the fish in hot oil until the skin is crisp and the flesh flakes, then drain on a rack.
Julienne the onion, carrot and peppers and slice the scotch bonnet thinly.
Bring the vinegar to a boil with pimento berries, sugar and salt, add the vegetables and cook two minutes so they stay crunchy.
Pour the hot pickle over the fried fish and leave at least twenty minutes before eating, or overnight.

recipes.name: Shrimp and Grits
steps: Cook the grits in salted water and milk over low heat for thirty minutes, whisking often so they never catch.
Beat butter and grated cheddar into the grits until they are loose, glossy and pourable.
Render the chopped bacon until crisp and lift it out, leaving the fat in the pan.
Toss the prawns with cayenne and sear them hard in the bacon fat for ninety seconds a side with the garlic.
Deglaze with a splash of stock and lemon juice, spoon the prawns over the grits and scatter bacon and spring onion.

recipes.name: Baked Mac and Cheese
steps: Boil the macaroni two minutes short of the packet time and drain it, since it will keep cooking in the oven.
Cook butter and flour into a blond roux, then whisk in the warm milk gradually until the sauce is thick and lump-free.
Off the heat beat in most of the grated cheddar, the mustard, smoked paprika, salt and plenty of pepper.
Fold the pasta through the sauce, which should look too loose, and tip it into a buttered dish.
Top with the rest of the cheese mixed with breadcrumbs and bake at 190C for twenty-five minutes until bubbling and crusted.

recipes.name: Crawfish Etouffee
steps: Melt the butter and stir in the flour, cooking it slowly to a peanut-butter coloured roux without burning it.
Tip in the chopped onion, celery and green pepper all at once and cook until they soften and the roux darkens.
Whisk in the warm stock a ladle at a time so the sauce stays smooth, then add the Cajun seasoning.
Simmer twenty-five minutes until the sauce is thick enough to mound on a spoon.
Fold in the crawfish tails for the last five minutes only, finish with spring onion and parsley and serve over rice.

recipes.name: Lauki Chana Dal
steps: Soak the chana dal for 20 minutes while you peel and cube the bottle gourd.
Pressure cook the dal with lauki, turmeric, salt and 2 cups water for 3 whistles.
Heat ghee, crackle cumin, fry onion till golden, add ginger and tomato and cook to a mash.
Fold the masala into the cooked dal, simmer 5 minutes so the gourd soaks up the flavour, and finish with coriander.

recipes.name: Beans Thoran
steps: Crush the coconut with shallots, green chilli and turmeric coarsely, without water.
Splutter mustard seeds and curry leaves in coconut oil.
Add the chopped beans with a splash of water and salt, cover and steam 6-8 minutes till just tender.
Stir in the coconut mix, cook uncovered 3 minutes so it stays dry and fragrant.

recipes.name: Cabbage Kootu
steps: Cook the moong dal with turmeric till soft and mashable.
Simmer the shredded cabbage in a little salted water till it loses its crunch.
Grind coconut, cumin and one red chilli to a paste and stir it into the dal with the cabbage.
Simmer 5 minutes, then pour over a tempering of mustard seeds, red chilli and asafoetida in coconut oil.

recipes.name: Paruppu Usili
steps: Soak both dals for 1 hour, then grind coarsely with red chilli, asafoetida and salt using no water.
Steam the ground paste for 10 minutes, cool, and crumble it between your fingers.
Boil the chopped beans in salted water till just tender and drain well.
Temper mustard and curry leaves in sesame oil, add the crumbled dal and roast till sandy, then fold in the beans and cook 5 more minutes.

recipes.name: Keerai Masiyal
steps: Cook the moong dal with turmeric till completely soft.
Add the washed greens to the hot dal, cover and cook 5 minutes till wilted.
Mash everything coarsely with a wooden masher so it stays rustic, not pureed.
Temper mustard seeds, crushed garlic, red chilli and asafoetida in sesame oil and pour over.

recipes.name: Kadalai Sundal
steps: Drain the boiled chickpeas well so the sundal does not turn soggy.
Splutter mustard seeds and urad dal in oil, then add red chilli, curry leaves and asafoetida.
Toss in the chickpeas with salt and stir on high heat for 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and mix in the fresh grated coconut.

recipes.name: Lobia Masala
steps: Pressure cook the soaked lobia with salt and turmeric for 3 whistles till tender but whole.
Brown the onion in hot oil, add ginger garlic paste and fry till the raw smell goes.
Add tomatoes and the dry spices and cook till the masala leaves oil at the edges.
Tip in the cooked lobia with its water, simmer 10 minutes, mash a few peas to thicken and finish with garam masala.

recipes.name: Tofu Bhurji
steps: Press the tofu for a few minutes and crumble it coarsely with your hands.
Fry onion and green chilli till soft, add tomato and cook 2 minutes.
Add turmeric, masala and salt, then the crumbled tofu, and toss on high heat for 4 minutes.
Squeeze in lemon, scatter coriander and serve hot with pav or roti.

recipes.name: Soya Keema Matar
steps: Soak the soya granules in hot salted water for 10 minutes, then squeeze them dry thoroughly.
Fry the onion till deep brown, add ginger garlic paste and the dry spices.
Add tomato puree and cook till thick, then stir in the squeezed granules and peas.
Add half a cup of water, cover and cook 10 minutes till the keema is dry and glossy, finish with garam masala and coriander.

recipes.name: Machher Jhol
steps: Rub the fish with turmeric and salt and rest 10 minutes, then shallow fry in smoking mustard oil till pale gold on both sides.
In the same oil crackle nigella seeds and green chilli, add potato and fry a minute.
Add ginger paste, tomato, turmeric and chilli powder with a splash of water and cook to a loose masala.
Pour in 2 cups hot water, simmer till the potato is done, slide the fish back in and cook 5 minutes more for a thin, spoonable jhol.

recipes.name: Meen Peera
steps: Crush the coconut with shallots, green chilli, turmeric and curry leaves lightly by hand.
Layer the cleaned fish in a clay pot or kadai with the coconut mix and soaked kudampuli.
Add half a cup of water and salt, cover and cook on low heat for 12 minutes without stirring.
Shake the pan to combine, drizzle coconut oil over the top and cook uncovered till almost dry.

recipes.name: Murgh Kali Mirch
steps: Marinate the chicken in yogurt, half the crushed pepper, ginger garlic paste and salt for 20 minutes.
Boil the onion and cashews for 8 minutes and blend to a smooth white paste.
Sear the chicken in ghee till it takes colour, then add the onion cashew paste and cook on low heat.
Add a little water, cover and cook 15 minutes, then finish with the remaining coarsely crushed pepper and slit green chillies.

recipes.name: Paneer Shashlik
steps: Whisk yogurt with tandoori masala, ginger garlic paste, lemon and salt into a thick marinade.
Fold in the paneer, capsicum and onion petals and rest 15 minutes.
Thread onto skewers alternating paneer and vegetables and grill on a hot tawa or in a 220C oven for 10 minutes.
Baste with butter, char the edges, and finish with chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.name: Ragi Roti
steps: Mix the ragi flour with onion, carrot, chilli, coriander, cumin and salt while dry.
Add warm water a little at a time to make a soft, just-holding dough and rest 5 minutes.
Pat a ball directly onto a greased tawa into a thin round with wet fingers and poke a few holes.
Drizzle oil around the edges, cover and cook on medium till the base is crisp, then flip for a minute.

recipes.name: Sambharo
steps: Heat oil till hazy and splutter mustard seeds with asafoetida and slit green chillies.
Add turmeric, then the shredded cabbage and carrot on the highest flame.
Toss for 3 to 4 minutes only, so the vegetables stay crunchy and bright.
Take off the heat, season with salt and sugar and finish with lemon juice.

recipes.name: Tomato Pappu
steps: Pressure cook the toor dal with chopped tomatoes, green chilli and turmeric for 4 whistles.
Whisk the cooked dal till the tomatoes melt into it and add salt and a little hot water.
Temper mustard seeds, cumin, red chilli, curry leaves and crushed garlic in oil till the garlic browns.
Pour the tempering over the dal, simmer 3 minutes and serve with steamed rice and ghee.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Erissery
steps: Cook the soaked cowpeas till tender, then add the pumpkin with turmeric, chilli powder and salt and cook till soft.
Grind half the coconut with cumin and a green chilli to a coarse paste and stir it in.
Mash the pumpkin lightly against the side of the pan and simmer 5 minutes.
Roast the remaining coconut in coconut oil with mustard seeds and curry leaves till deep brown and fold it through.

recipes.name: Tandoori Jhinga
steps: Toss the prawns with lemon, salt and half the chilli powder and rest 10 minutes.
Whisk hung curd with ginger garlic paste, ajwain, remaining chilli powder and mustard oil and coat the prawns.
Skewer and grill over high heat or on a smoking hot griddle for 3 minutes a side, no longer.
Dust with chaat masala and serve with sliced onion and mint chutney.

recipes.name: Egg Kejriwal
steps: Mix the grated cheese with minced green chilli, onion, pepper and a pinch of salt.
Spread thickly on buttered bread and grill or tawa-toast till the cheese blisters.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in butter, keeping the yolks runny.
Slide an egg onto each cheese toast, crack over more pepper and eat immediately.

recipes.name: Varan Bhaat
steps: Pressure cook the toor dal with turmeric and plenty of water till completely soft.
Whisk the dal smooth, add salt, a pinch of asafoetida and jaggery and bring to a gentle boil.
Steam the rice separately so the grains stay separate.
Mound the rice, ladle the varan over it, add a spoon of hot ghee and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.name: Lemon Coriander Soup
steps: Sweat the minced garlic and chopped coriander stems in a teaspoon of oil.
Add the stock, carrot and cabbage and simmer 6 minutes till just tender.
Stir in cornflour slurry and soy sauce and cook till the soup turns glossy.
Take off the heat, add lemon juice, crushed pepper and a fistful of chopped coriander leaves.

recipes.name: Buta no Shogayaki
steps: Whisk grated ginger with soy sauce, mirin and sake and marinate the pork slices for 10 minutes.
Sear the pork in a hot pan in a single layer, one minute a side, and set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan, pour in the leftover marinade and reduce till syrupy.
Return the pork, toss to glaze, and serve over finely shredded raw cabbage with rice.

recipes.name: Saba Shioyaki
steps: Pat the mackerel dry, splash with sake, and salt both sides generously; rest 10 minutes and wipe off the moisture that beads up.
Score the skin twice and grill skin side first under a hot broiler or on a griddle for 6 minutes.
Turn and cook the flesh side 4 minutes till just set and the skin is blistered.
Serve with a mound of grated daikon dressed with a few drops of soy sauce and a lemon wedge.

recipes.name: Chawanmushi
steps: Beat the eggs gently without frothing and mix with cooled dashi, soy sauce and mirin in a 1:3 ratio.
Strain the mixture twice through a fine sieve for a glassy set.
Divide prawns, chicken and sliced shiitake between cups and pour the custard over.
Cover the cups and steam on low heat for 12 to 14 minutes until just barely set with a faint wobble.

recipes.name: Kenchinjiru
steps: Crumble the tofu by hand and fry it in sesame oil till the edges dry out.
Add the daikon, carrot and burdock cut into rough bite-sized pieces and stir-fry 4 minutes.
Pour in the kombu dashi, skim, and simmer 15 minutes till the root vegetables are tender.
Season with soy sauce and a pinch of salt and finish with sliced spring onion.

recipes.name: Yum Woon Sen
steps: Soak the glass noodles in hot water till pliable, then blanch 30 seconds and drain cold.
Poach the prawns and minced pork in the same water for a minute each until just cooked.
Pound chilli and garlic and whisk with lime juice, fish sauce and a little palm sugar.
Toss noodles, seafood, sliced shallot, celery and coriander with the dressing and top with crushed peanuts.

recipes.name: Canh Chua Ca
steps: Dissolve the tamarind in a cup of hot water and strain out the seeds.
Bring 5 cups of water to a boil with tamarind liquid, tomato and pineapple and simmer 5 minutes.
Slide in the fish steaks and sliced okra and poach gently for 8 minutes without stirring.
Season with fish sauce and sugar, throw in bean sprouts and herbs, and take off the heat at once.

recipes.name: Goi Ga
steps: Salt the shredded cabbage for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water so the salad stays crisp.
Whisk lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, minced garlic and chilli into a sharp nuoc cham.
Toss the chicken, cabbage, carrot and torn mint with the dressing just before serving.
Scatter over fried shallots and crushed peanuts for crunch.

recipes.name: Tinolang Manok
steps: Fry the ginger, garlic and onion in oil till fragrant and lightly coloured.
Add the chicken pieces and sear, then splash in fish sauce and let it sizzle for a minute.
Pour in the rice washing water or stock and simmer 20 minutes, skimming the top.
Add the wedges of green papaya, cook till translucent, then wilt in the leaves and finish with cracked pepper.

recipes.name: Kongnamul Guk
steps: Steep the kombu in 5 cups of cold water, bring almost to a boil and remove it.
Add the rinsed soybean sprouts and boil with the lid firmly on for 8 minutes without lifting it, or the soup will smell raw.
Season with soy sauce, salt and minced garlic and simmer 3 minutes more.
Finish with gochugaru, spring onion and sesame seeds; serve scalding hot with rice.

recipes.name: Miyeok Guk
steps: Soak the dried seaweed in cold water for 20 minutes till it swells, then rinse and cut into short lengths.
Fry the diced beef in sesame oil till it browns, add garlic and a splash of soy sauce.
Add the seaweed and stir-fry two minutes so it takes on the fat, then pour in 6 cups of water.
Simmer 20 minutes till the broth turns milky, season with fish sauce and salt, and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Sayur Asem
steps: Grind the shallots, garlic, galangal and red chilli into a rough paste.
Boil the paste with 6 cups of water, bay leaf and the raw peanuts for 12 minutes till the peanuts soften.
Add corn and chayote and cook 8 minutes, then the long beans for 3 minutes.
Stir in tamarind water, palm sugar and salt and balance it so the soup is sour first, sweet second.

recipes.name: Winter Melon Soup
steps: Blanch the pork ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes and rinse away the scum.
Simmer the ribs with ginger, soaked shiitake and 7 cups of water for 30 minutes.
Add the cubed winter melon and cook 15 minutes till it turns translucent.
Add goji berries, season with salt and white pepper, and scatter spring onion over each bowl.

recipes.name: Avgolemono
steps: Simmer the chicken with onion and celery in 6 cups of water for 25 minutes, then lift out the meat, shred it and strain the broth.
Cook the rice in the simmering broth till soft.
Whisk the eggs with lemon juice, then temper by trickling in hot broth while whisking constantly.
Pour the egg-lemon mixture back into the pot off the heat, stir till velvety, return the chicken and finish with dill; never let it boil again.

recipes.name: Gigantes Plaki
steps: Boil the soaked beans for 35 minutes till tender but still holding shape, and save a cup of the water.
Soften onion, carrot and garlic in a generous amount of olive oil, then add passata and oregano and simmer 10 minutes.
Combine beans and sauce with the reserved water in a baking dish and season well.
Bake at 190C for 35 minutes till the top caramelises and the sauce thickens; stir through parsley and eat warm, not hot.

recipes.name: Fasolada
steps: Boil the soaked beans in fresh water for 20 minutes and drain.
Sweat onion, diced carrot and celery in half the olive oil till glossy, then stir in the tomato paste.
Return the beans with 5 cups of water and the bay leaf and simmer 25 minutes till creamy.
Season late so the beans stay soft, pour in the remaining raw olive oil and a splash of vinegar off the heat.

recipes.name: Ezogelin Corbasi
steps: Fry the chopped onion in butter till soft, then cook the tomato and pepper pastes in it for a minute.
Add the washed red lentils, bulgur and rice with 6 cups of water and simmer 25 minutes till everything collapses.
Blend briefly or leave rustic, then adjust with hot water to a pourable consistency.
Sizzle dried mint and chilli flakes in a spoon of butter and swirl it in; serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Kisir
steps: Pour an equal volume of boiling water over the fine bulgur, cover and leave 15 minutes till fluffy.
Rub the pepper paste, olive oil, pomegranate molasses and lemon juice into the warm bulgur with your hands.
Fold in finely chopped spring onion, parsley, tomato and chilli flakes.
Check the balance for sour and salt and serve on lettuce leaves at room temperature.

recipes.name: Balila
steps: Warm the chickpeas gently in a little of their own cooking liquid so they stay whole and soft.
Mash the garlic with salt into a paste and whisk with cumin and lemon juice.
Pour the dressing over the hot chickpeas and stir so they drink it in.
Ladle into bowls with some of the broth, pour olive oil over and scatter parsley and more cumin.

recipes.name: Loubieh bi Zeit
steps: Top and tail the beans and snap them into finger lengths.
Soften the sliced onion in plenty of olive oil, then add the garlic and ground coriander.
Add the tomatoes and cook till they break down into a loose sauce.
Add the beans with a splash of water, cover, and stew on low heat for 25 minutes till completely soft; serve at room temperature with bread.

recipes.name: Shopska Salad
steps: Roast the pepper over a flame till blackened, peel and cut into strips.
Chop the tomato, cucumber and onion into even chunks and season with salt.
Dress with oil and vinegar and toss with the pepper and parsley.
Grate a thick blanket of white brine cheese over the top so the salad disappears beneath it.

recipes.name: Panzanella
steps: Tear the stale bread into chunks and soak briefly in water, then squeeze almost dry.
Chop the tomatoes over a bowl so all the juice is caught, and salt them for 10 minutes.
Soak the sliced red onion in the vinegar to take the bite out.
Toss bread, tomatoes with their juice, cucumber, onion and torn basil with olive oil and let it sit 10 minutes before eating.

recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
steps: Make a soffritto of finely diced onion, carrot and celery in olive oil over low heat for 10 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and rosemary, then two thirds of the beans with 4 cups of water.
Blend the remaining beans smooth and stir them in so the soup thickens without cream.
Cook the pasta directly in the soup till al dente, rest 5 minutes off the heat and finish each bowl with raw olive oil and pepper.

recipes.name: Stracciatella alla Romana
steps: Beat the eggs with parmesan, semolina, nutmeg and a little cold broth till smooth.
Bring the rest of the broth to a bare simmer, never a rolling boil.
Pour in the egg mixture in a thin stream while stirring with a fork so it sets into ragged threads.
Cook one more minute, season, and serve with parsley and extra parmesan.

recipes.name: Cobb Salad
steps: Crisp the bacon in a dry pan and drain on paper, then crumble it.
Season and grill the chicken breast, rest it 5 minutes and slice thickly.
Lay the chopped lettuce flat and arrange chicken, bacon, quartered eggs, avocado, tomatoes and blue cheese in tidy stripes.
Pour the vinaigrette over at the table and toss only once everyone has seen it.

recipes.name: Turkey Chili
steps: Brown the minced turkey hard in a dry heavy pot so it takes real colour, then set aside.
Cook the onion and garlic in the same pot, add cumin, paprika and chipotle and toast 30 seconds.
Return the turkey with tomatoes, beans and stock and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes.
Season, let it thicken, and serve with lime, coriander and a spoon of yogurt or sour cream.

recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
steps: Simmer the chicken thighs in the stock with bay leaf and thyme for 20 minutes, then shred the meat off the bone.
Sweat the diced onion, carrot and celery in butter till they soften but keep their shape.
Return the broth and shredded chicken and simmer 5 minutes.
Cook the noodles separately so they do not swell in the pot, add them to the bowls and ladle the soup over; finish with parsley and pepper.

recipes.name: Salmon en Papillote
steps: Cut two large hearts of baking parchment and butter the centres.
Make a bed of julienned leek and shaved fennel on each, sit the salmon on top and season.
Add lemon slices, herbs, a knob of butter and a splash of wine, then fold and crimp the edges tightly into a sealed parcel.
Bake at 200C for 12 to 14 minutes until the parcel puffs, and let each person tear theirs open at the table.

recipes.name: Cuban Black Bean Soup
steps: Simmer the soaked black beans with bay leaves and one halved capsicum for 40 minutes till soft.
Make a sofrito by frying finely chopped onion, the rest of the capsicum and garlic in olive oil with cumin and oregano.
Stir the sofrito into the beans, mash a ladleful against the pot to thicken, and simmer 10 minutes.
Sharpen with vinegar and a pinch of sugar at the end and serve over white rice with raw onion on top.

recipes.name: Split Pea Soup
steps: Soften the diced onion, carrot and celery in olive oil with thyme and smoked paprika.
Add the rinsed split peas, bay leaf and 7 cups of water and bring to a boil.
Simmer partly covered for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally, till the peas collapse into a thick puree.
Blend half the soup for body, season generously, and loosen with hot water before serving with croutons.

recipes.name: Kuttu ki Puri
steps: Bind the buckwheat flour with curd, grated ginger, chopped chilli and rock salt into a soft dough — it will feel stickier than wheat dough.
Rest it ten minutes, then roll small puris between two sheets of greased plastic rather than on a floured board.
Slide each puri into hot ghee and press it down gently with a slotted spoon until it puffs.
Turn once, fry to a deep tan and drain; serve hot with vrat aloo or curd.

recipes.name: Singhare ke Atte ka Paratha
steps: Squeeze the grated bottle gourd dry and knead it into the singhara flour with chilli, coriander and rock salt.
The dough holds together poorly, so pat each ball flat by hand on a greased sheet instead of rolling.
Cook on a hot tawa with ghee, pressing the edges down until both sides are freckled brown.
Serve immediately with thick curd — these go leathery as they cool.

recipes.name: Rajgira Paratha
steps: Work the amaranth flour into a pliable dough with curd, cumin, chopped chilli and rock salt.
Divide into balls and flatten each between greased plastic sheets to about 5 mm.
Griddle on medium with ghee until both faces carry dark spots.
Amaranth is the most protein-dense of the fasting flours — serve with curd for a full meal.

recipes.name: Samak Rice Khichdi
steps: Rinse the samak twice and soak it fifteen minutes while you cube the potato.
Temper cumin and slit chillies in ghee, add the potato and turn it until the edges go translucent.
Add the drained samak, crushed peanuts, rock salt and two and a half cups of water.
Cover and cook twelve minutes until the grain bursts and the khichdi is loose but not soupy.

recipes.name: Samak Pulao with Peanuts
steps: Dry-roast the peanuts until the skins blister, rub them off and crush coarsely.
Temper ginger and curry leaves in ghee, add soaked samak and toss for a minute.
Pour in two cups of water with rock salt, cover and cook till the grain opens.
Fork through the peanuts and raw diced cucumber off the heat so it stays crisp.

recipes.name: Farali Dhokla
steps: Whisk samak and sabudana flour into curd with the chilli-ginger paste and rock salt; rest twenty minutes.
Stir in fruit salt with a splash of water and pour at once into a greased tin.
Steam fifteen minutes until a skewer comes out clean, then cool before cutting into squares.
Finish with a tempering of cumin, sesame and curry leaves in ghee.

recipes.name: Sabudana Thalipeeth
steps: Soak the sabudana six hours until a pearl crushes cleanly between two fingers, then drain thoroughly.
Mix with mashed potato, crushed peanuts, chopped chilli, coriander and rock salt.
Pat the mixture directly onto a greased tawa into a rough disc with wet fingers, making a hole in the centre.
Drizzle ghee into the hole and around the edge and cook covered until the underside is crisp; flip once.

recipes.name: Makhana Kheer
steps: Roast the makhana in ghee until they crackle and turn brittle, then crush half of them coarsely.
Reduce the milk by a third on a low flame, stirring so it does not catch.
Add both the whole and crushed makhana and simmer fifteen minutes until they swell and thicken the milk.
Sweeten, add crushed cardamom and slivered nuts, and serve warm or chilled.

recipes.name: Roasted Makhana Namkeen
steps: Roast the makhana dry on a low flame for eight minutes until one snaps cleanly rather than bending.
Add ghee and curry leaves and toss another two minutes so every piece is coated.
Season with rock salt and coarsely cracked pepper off the heat.
Cool completely before storing or they go soft within the hour.

recipes.name: Vrat ke Jeera Aloo
steps: Break the boiled potatoes by hand into rough chunks — torn edges hold the tempering better than knife cuts.
Crackle plenty of cumin in ghee, then add slit chillies and julienned ginger.
Fold in the potato with rock salt and let it sit undisturbed two minutes to catch colour.
Finish with lemon and a heavy hand of coriander.

recipes.name: Vrat Wale Dahi Aloo
steps: Whisk the singhara flour into the curd until no lumps remain — this is what stops it splitting.
Temper cumin, chilli and ginger in ghee and add the roughly broken potatoes.
Lower the heat, pour in the curd mixture and stir continuously in one direction until it comes to a bare simmer.
Season with rock salt and cook five minutes more until glossy and lightly thickened.

recipes.name: Arbi ki Sookhi Sabzi
steps: Boil the arbi just until a knife slides in, then peel and press each one flat with your palm.
Shallow fry the flattened pieces in ghee without crowding until the cut faces are crisp and golden.
Add carom seeds, slit chillies and cracked pepper and toss for a minute.
Season with rock salt and a squeeze of lemon, which also cuts arbi's slipperiness.

recipes.name: Vrat ki Kaddu Sabzi
steps: Cube the pumpkin with its skin on — it holds the pieces together as they soften.
Crackle cumin and a few fenugreek seeds in ghee, add slit chillies.
Add the pumpkin with rock salt and a splash of water, cover and cook till it collapses at the edges.
Mash a third of it into the pan and finish with lemon so it lands sweet-sour rather than merely sweet.

recipes.name: Lauki ka Halwa
steps: Squeeze the grated bottle gourd lightly and sauté it in ghee until the raw smell goes and it turns glassy.
Pour in the milk and simmer on low, stirring often, until almost all of it is absorbed.
Add sugar — it will loosen the halwa again — and keep cooking until it pulls away from the pan.
Fold in cardamom and ghee-fried cashews and raisins.

recipes.name: Singhare ke Atte ka Halwa
steps: Roast the singhara flour in ghee on a low flame for a full ten minutes — it darkens slowly and burns fast.
Boil the water with sugar and cardamom separately and keep it hot.
Pour the syrup into the roasted flour in one go, standing back from the steam, and stir hard to break lumps.
Cook until the halwa leaves the sides and pools ghee, then fold in slivered almonds.

recipes.name: Rajgira Sheera
steps: Roast the amaranth flour in ghee until it smells nutty and loosens from the pan.
Warm the milk with jaggery until dissolved, then add it slowly to the flour while stirring.
Cook three or four minutes until thick and glossy.
Finish with cardamom and fried cashews; eat warm, as amaranth stiffens on cooling.

recipes.name: Sabudana Kheer
steps: Soak the sabudana thirty minutes only — longer and the pearls dissolve into paste in the milk.
Simmer the milk with saffron until it reduces by a quarter.
Add the drained sabudana and cook on low, stirring often, until every pearl is clear.
Sweeten at the end, add cardamom, and rest ten minutes before serving so it thickens properly.

recipes.name: Vrat ki Kadhi
steps: Whisk the singhara flour into the curd with three cups of water until completely smooth.
Bring it to a boil stirring constantly, then drop to the lowest flame and cook twenty minutes.
In a separate spoon, crackle cumin, slit chillies and curry leaves in ghee.
Pour the tempering over the kadhi, season with rock salt and cover for a minute before serving.

recipes.name: Samak Idli
steps: Grind soaked samak with curd to a thick idli-batter consistency and rest it twenty minutes.
Stir in grated ginger, minced chilli and rock salt.
Add fruit salt with a spoon of water, fold gently and pour into greased idli moulds at once.
Steam ten to twelve minutes; a skewer should come out dry. Serve with peanut chutney.

recipes.name: Kuttu ka Dosa
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour with curd and enough water to make a thin, pourable batter; rest fifteen minutes.
Stir in cumin, chopped chilli, coriander and rock salt — the batter thickens as it sits, so loosen it again.
Pour a ladleful onto a hot greased tawa and spread thin from the centre outwards.
Drizzle ghee around the rim and cook until the edges lift; buckwheat crisps but does not brown much.

recipes.name: Farali Pattice
steps: Mash the potatoes smooth with sabudana flour and rock salt to make a dough that holds a shape.
Make the filling by mixing coconut, crushed peanuts, chilli, coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
Flatten a portion of potato dough in your palm, spoon in the filling and seal into a patty.
Shallow fry in ghee on medium until a hard golden crust forms on both faces.

recipes.name: Shengdana Amti
steps: Roast the peanuts, rub off the skins and grind two-thirds of them with coconut and chilli to a coarse paste.
Temper cumin in ghee, add the paste and fry until it darkens and the ghee separates at the edges.
Add three cups of water, the reserved whole peanuts, jaggery and rock salt.
Simmer fifteen minutes until the amti thickens slightly and tastes hot, sweet and nutty at once.

recipes.name: Upvasachi Bhaji
steps: Crackle cumin and slit green chillies in ghee — this bhaji is meant to be properly hot.
Add cubed boiled potato and crushed roasted peanuts and toss to coat.
Season with rock salt and let it sit on the heat until the base catches slightly.
Finish with grated coconut and lemon off the flame.

recipes.name: Rajgira Ladoo
steps: Melt the jaggery with a splash of water and ghee and cook to a soft-ball stage — a drop should set firm in cold water.
Take it off the heat, add cardamom and tip in the puffed amaranth.
Mix fast; the syrup sets within a minute.
Grease your palms and roll into ladoos while still warm.

recipes.name: Makhana Raita
steps: Roast the makhana until crisp and break them into halves.
Whisk the curd smooth with rock salt and roasted ground cumin.
Fold in the makhana just before serving so they keep some bite.
Top with minced chilli and coriander.

recipes.name: Vrat Wala Kheera Kachumber
steps: Dice the cucumber small and keep it cold until the moment of mixing.
Crush the roasted peanuts coarsely — powder makes the salad claggy.
Toss cucumber, peanuts, coconut, minced chilli and coriander with lemon and rock salt.
Serve within a few minutes; the cucumber weeps and dilutes it if it stands.

recipes.name: Kacche Kele ki Sabzi
steps: Boil the raw bananas whole for eight minutes, cool, peel and cut into thick rounds.
Fry the rounds in ghee in a single layer until the faces are golden and slightly crusted.
Add carom, slit chilli and cracked pepper and toss for a minute.
Season with rock salt and lemon and serve straight away.

recipes.name: Kele ke Kofte
steps: Mash the boiled raw banana with singhara flour, ginger and rock salt and roll into small koftas.
Fry them in ghee until firm and browned all over, then set aside on paper.
Blend the tomatoes and cook the purée in ghee with chilli until it thickens and darkens.
Whisk in the curd off the heat, return to a bare simmer, then slip the koftas in just before serving so they stay whole.

recipes.name: Vrat ka Paneer
steps: Blend tomatoes with soaked cashews, ginger and green chilli to a smooth purée.
Cook the purée in ghee on medium for ten minutes until it darkens and the ghee pools at the edges.
Season with rock salt, loosen with a little water and stir in cream.
Add cubed paneer at the very end and warm through only — boiling it turns paneer rubbery.

recipes.name: Singhare ki Barfi
steps: Roast the singhara flour in ghee on low until it turns a shade darker and smells toasted.
Add crumbled khoya and keep stirring until it melts into the flour.
Stir in sugar; the mixture loosens, then thickens again — cook until it holds a line drawn with the spoon.
Press into a greased tray, scatter pistachios, cool completely and cut into diamonds.

recipes.name: Vrat Wale Dahi Vade
steps: Whisk samak flour with a little curd and water into a thick dropping batter and rest it fifteen minutes.
Drop spoonfuls into hot ghee and fry until firm and golden, then soak them in warm salted water for five minutes.
Squeeze each vada gently between your palms to press out the water.
Sit them in whisked chilled curd and finish with roasted cumin, rock salt, chilli and coriander.

recipes.name: Vrat ki Aloo Tikki
steps: Grate the boiled potatoes rather than mashing them — the tikki stays lighter.
Bind with singhara flour, crushed peanuts, chilli, coriander and rock salt.
Shape thick patties and chill them fifteen minutes so they hold on the pan.
Shallow fry in ghee, undisturbed, until a hard crust forms before turning.

recipes.name: Kaddu ka Halwa
steps: Sauté the grated pumpkin in ghee until it loses its raw edge and deepens in colour.
Add milk and cook down on a medium flame, stirring, until nearly dry.
Stir in sugar and keep going until the halwa glistens and holds together.
Finish with cardamom and toasted almond slivers.

recipes.name: Sabudana Tikki
steps: Drain the soaked sabudana completely — wet pearls make the tikki burst in the pan.
Mix with mashed potato, crushed peanuts, chilli, lemon and rock salt.
Shape into small thick discs and rest them ten minutes.
Shallow fry on a medium flame until translucent and crisp on both sides.

recipes.name: Kuttu ka Chilla
steps: Whisk the buckwheat flour to a thin batter with water, then fold in grated bottle gourd.
Add minced chilli, coriander and rock salt and rest ten minutes.
Ladle onto a hot greased tawa and spread to a thick pancake rather than a thin crepe.
Cook covered two minutes, drizzle ghee, flip and finish; serve with curd.

recipes.name: Phool Makhana Curry
steps: Roast the makhana in a spoon of ghee until crisp and set aside.
Blend tomato with soaked cashews, ginger and chilli and cook the purée in ghee till it thickens.
Whisk in the curd on a low flame so it does not split, then add water to gravy consistency.
Drop the makhana in three minutes before serving — any longer and they go spongy.

recipes.name: Sweet Potato Chaat
steps: Roast the sweet potatoes whole over an open flame or in an oven until the skin blisters and the flesh gives.
Peel and cut into thick cubes while still warm.
Toss with lemon juice, roasted cumin, minced chilli and rock salt.
Scatter coriander and eat warm — this is a winter street snack and it dies cold.

recipes.name: Samak ke Chawal ki Kheer
steps: Roast the samak in a touch of ghee for two minutes so the grains stay separate.
Simmer it in the milk on a low flame, stirring every few minutes, until the grain swells and the milk thickens.
Add sugar only near the end, or the grain stops softening.
Finish with cardamom and slivered almonds; it thickens further as it cools.

recipes.name: Vrat Wali Arbi Tikki
steps: Grate the boiled peeled arbi and squeeze out as much moisture as you can.
Bind with singhara flour, carom, minced chilli, coriander and rock salt.
Shape into small flat tikkis and chill them so they firm up.
Shallow fry in ghee until deeply crusted; arbi browns slower than potato, so give it time.

recipes.name: Sama Pulao with Pumpkin
steps: Crackle cumin in ghee with slit chilli and julienned ginger.
Add the pumpkin cubes and cook until their edges soften and colour.
Stir in the soaked samak with rock salt and two cups of water.
Cover and cook twelve minutes, then rest off the heat five minutes before forking through.

recipes.name: Farali Chivda
steps: Rinse the grated potato straws until the water runs clear, then dry them completely on a cloth.
Fry them in batches in hot ghee until pale gold and crisp; they darken after draining.
Fry peanuts, makhana, slit chillies and curry leaves separately and drain.
Toss everything with rock salt and a pinch of sugar and cool fully before storing.

recipes.name: Vrat ka Tamatar Shorba
steps: Boil the tomatoes with ginger, chilli and three cups of water until the skins slip.
Blend and pass through a sieve for a clean-tasting shorba.
Crackle cumin in ghee, whisk in the singhara flour for ten seconds, then pour in the purée.
Simmer until it just coats a spoon, season with rock salt and finish with coriander.

recipes.name: Vrat Wale Sabudana Papad Rolls
steps: Mash the drained sabudana with boiled potato and rock salt into a workable dough.
Make a filling of coconut, minced chilli, coriander and a squeeze of lemon.
Flatten a portion of dough, lay a line of filling along it and roll into a cylinder, sealing the ends.
Shallow fry the rolls slowly, turning, until translucent and evenly crisp.

recipes.name: Rajgira Kheer
steps: Reduce the milk by a quarter on a low flame with the cardamom.
Stir in the puffed amaranth and cook eight minutes until it swells and thickens the milk.
Take the pan off the heat before adding jaggery, or the milk will split.
Return briefly to a bare simmer, add fried cashews and serve warm.

recipes.name: Vrat ka Fruit Raita
steps: Whisk the curd smooth with sugar, a pinch of rock salt and crushed cardamom.
Dice the apple and banana just before mixing so they do not brown or turn mushy.
Fold the fruit and pomegranate through the curd.
Chill twenty minutes; do not make it more than an hour ahead.

recipes.name: Hing Wale Aloo
steps: Heat mustard oil until it stops smoking, then drop in asafoetida and cumin.
Add hand-crushed boiled potatoes and turn them in the oil so the broken faces catch.
Sprinkle turmeric, chilli powder and salt and cook without stirring for two minutes at a time.
Finish with amchur, which does the job onion and garlic would otherwise do here.

recipes.name: Vaishnav Dal
steps: Pressure-cook the toor dal with turmeric until it collapses, then whisk it smooth.
Temper cumin, asafoetida, curry leaves, slit chilli and grated ginger in oil.
Pour the tempering into the dal with chopped tomato, jaggery and salt.
Simmer fifteen minutes — asafoetida and ginger carry this dal where onion and garlic normally would.

recipes.name: Mor Kuzhambu
steps: Grind coconut, cumin and green chilli to a fine paste with a little water.
Whisk the paste and rice flour into the sour curd with turmeric and salt.
Heat it gently, stirring in one direction, and take it off the moment it steams — it must never boil.
Temper mustard seeds and curry leaves in coconut oil and pour over.

recipes.name: Temple Style Puliyodarai
steps: Extract thick tamarind pulp and reduce it in sesame oil with asafoetida until it darkens and thickens to a paste.
Roast and grind sesame seeds with a couple of dried chillies to a coarse powder.
Temper peanuts, dried chillies and curry leaves in sesame oil and fold into cooled cooked rice.
Mix in the tamarind paste and the sesame powder and rest an hour — it improves markedly as it sits.

recipes.name: Satvik Paneer Curry
steps: Blend tomatoes with soaked cashews and ginger to a smooth purée.
Bloom asafoetida in ghee for a few seconds — it is doing the work of the onion and garlic, so do not skip it.
Cook the purée in the ghee for twelve minutes until it darkens and thickens.
Season, stir in cream and crushed kasuri methi, then add the paneer and warm through without boiling.

recipes.name: Jain Pav Bhaji
steps: Boiled raw banana stands in for potato here and mashes to the same texture — mash it with the peas.
Cook chopped tomato and capsicum in plenty of butter until entirely broken down.
Add the masala and the mash and keep mashing on the heat until the bhaji is uniform and glossy.
Finish with a lump of butter, lemon and a heap of coriander; serve with buttered pav.

recipes.name: Hing Jeera Kadhi
steps: Whisk besan into the sour curd with turmeric and four cups of water until absolutely smooth.
Bring to a boil stirring constantly, then simmer on the lowest flame for thirty minutes — the long cook is what makes kadhi taste of anything.
Temper asafoetida, cumin, fenugreek and dried chillies in ghee until the chillies darken.
Pour the tempering in, season, and cover for five minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Niramish Aloo Dum
steps: Parboil, peel and prick the baby potatoes, then fry them in mustard oil until blistered.
Temper panch phoron, bay leaf and asafoetida in the same oil.
Add ginger paste and chopped tomato with chilli powder and cook until the oil separates.
Return the potatoes with a cup of water, cover and cook on low until the gravy clings — no onion or garlic anywhere in this.

recipes.name: Sukhi Chana Dal
steps: Soak the chana dal two hours, then cook it with turmeric and salt until each grain is tender but still whole and separate.
Drain any remaining water — this dal is meant to be dry.
Temper asafoetida, cumin, julienned ginger and slit chilli in ghee.
Fold the dal through the tempering, cook two minutes and finish with coriander and lemon.

recipes.name: Bhindi Sambhariya
steps: Roast the besan dry until it smells nutty, then mix it with coconut, coriander, chilli, sugar and salt to make the sambharo.
Slit each okra lengthways without cutting through and pack the filling in.
Lay them in a wide pan with hot oil and asafoetida in a single layer.
Cover and cook on low, turning gently every few minutes, until the okra is tender and the stuffing has crusted.

recipes.name: Udupi Sambar
steps: Roast coriander seeds, dried chillies and a spoon of chana dal in coconut oil, then grind with fresh coconut to a fine paste.
Cook the toor dal soft and cook the ash gourd separately in tamarind water until just done.
Combine dal, vegetable, ground paste, jaggery and salt and simmer fifteen minutes.
Temper mustard seeds, asafoetida and curry leaves in coconut oil and pour over — no onion or garlic in the Udupi kitchen.

recipes.name: Kootu
steps: Cook the moong dal and the cubed gourd together with turmeric until both are soft.
Grind coconut, cumin and green chilli to a smooth paste.
Stir the paste into the dal with salt and simmer five minutes, no more, so the coconut stays sweet.
Temper mustard seeds, asafoetida and curry leaves in coconut oil and pour over.

recipes.name: Gujarati Toor Dal
steps: Cook the toor dal very soft and whisk it thin — Gujarati dal is a drinking consistency, not a stew.
Add tamarind pulp, jaggery, raw peanuts, salt and enough water to loosen it.
Simmer twenty minutes so the peanuts soften and the sweet and sour settle into each other.
Temper mustard seeds, asafoetida, curry leaves and slit chilli in oil and pour in.

recipes.name: Rasawala Bateta Nu Shaak
steps: Crackle mustard seeds and asafoetida in oil, add slit chillies and chopped tomato.
Add hand-broken boiled potato with turmeric and salt and mash a few pieces into the pan.
Pour in two cups of water with jaggery and simmer until it thickens into a thin gravy.
Finish with coriander and lemon; this is the classic Gujarati breakfast shaak eaten with puri.

recipes.name: Satvik Khichdi
steps: Dry-roast the moong dal for two minutes until it smells faintly nutty, then rinse with the rice.
Temper cumin, asafoetida and grated ginger in ghee in a pressure cooker.
Add rice, dal, turmeric, salt and four cups of water and cook to three whistles.
Whisk in more hot water to a soft porridge, crack pepper over and add a final spoon of ghee.

recipes.name: Panchamrit Sabzi
steps: Dry-roast peanuts, sesame and coconut separately until each is fragrant, then grind coarsely together.
Temper asafoetida and broken dried chillies in oil.
Add the ground mixture with tamarind pulp, jaggery, salt and half a cup of water.
Cook five minutes until it comes together as a thick relish-like sabzi — sweet, sour, hot and nutty at once.

recipes.name: Gochujang Butter Beans
steps: Warm the sesame oil in a wide pan and fry the sliced garlic for a minute until it smells sweet rather than browned.
Stir in the gochujang and tomato puree and cook two minutes so the paste loses its raw edge and darkens.
Tip in the drained butter beans with a splash of their liquid, simmer five minutes, then fold through the spinach until it collapses.

recipes.name: Harissa Chickpea Traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and tip the drained chickpeas onto a tray with the onion cut into wedges and the pepper sliced thick.
Toss everything with the harissa and olive oil until the chickpeas are properly coated, then push them into a single layer.
Roast twenty minutes, scattering the cherry tomatoes over for the last eight so they blister instead of collapsing.
Scrape the sticky caramelised bits off the tray back through the chickpeas before serving.

recipes.name: Chilli Crisp Eggs
steps: Spoon a tablespoon of the oil from the chilli crisp jar into a cold non-stick pan and set it over a medium-high heat.
Crack in the eggs and let the whites bubble and frill at the edges while the yolks stay loose, about three minutes.
Slide them out, spoon over the chilli crisp solids, then splash the soy and vinegar into the hot pan and pour that over with the sliced spring onions.

recipes.name: Miso Butter Salmon Traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and mash the soft butter with the miso and mirin into a loose paste.
Lay the salmon and broccoli on a lined tray, dot the miso butter over both and toss the broccoli so it is glossy.
Roast twelve to fourteen minutes until the salmon flakes at the thickest point and the broccoli tips have caught.
Spoon the melted miso butter from the tray back over the fish and finish with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Za'atar Chicken Thighs
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and rub the thighs with half the za'atar, the olive oil and a good pinch of salt.
Scatter the onion wedges and thick courgette half-moons around them on the tray, skin side of the chicken up.
Roast twenty-two minutes without turning, so the skin dries and crisps while the vegetables soften underneath.
Squeeze the lemon over the hot tray and shower with the rest of the za'atar just before it goes to the table.

recipes.name: Tahini Noodles
steps: Boil the noodles, dropping the frozen edamame in for the last two minutes, then save a mug of the water before draining.
Whisk the tahini, soy, vinegar and grated garlic in the empty pan, loosening with the starchy water until it pours like cream.
Return the noodles and edamame and toss over a low heat until the sauce clings rather than pools, adding more water if it tightens.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Baked Eggs
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and spread the cottage cheese across a small oiled baking dish with the spinach folded through it.
Make four dips with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each, seasoning the yolks lightly.
Bake twelve to fourteen minutes until the whites are set but the yolks still wobble.
Scatter with chilli flakes and torn dill and eat straight from the dish.

recipes.name: Kimchi Grilled Cheese
steps: Squeeze the kimchi hard over the sink so it does not steam the sandwich, then chop it roughly with the spring onion.
Butter the outsides of both slices and build the sandwich with cheese, kimchi, then more cheese so the kimchi is sealed in.
Cook in a dry pan over a medium-low heat, pressed under a plate, for four minutes a side until deep gold and molten.

recipes.name: Paneer Tacos with Pickled Onion
steps: Slice the onion into fine rings and squeeze over the juice of one lime with a pinch of salt so it pickles while you cook.
Cube the paneer, toss it with the chipotle paste, and fry in a hot dry pan for six minutes until the edges blacken in patches.
Warm the tortillas in the same pan for twenty seconds a side.
Load with paneer, the drained pink onions, coriander and a squeeze from the second lime.

recipes.name: Chipotle Tofu Traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 220C, press the tofu briefly between kitchen paper and tear it into rough chunks so the edges catch.
Toss the tofu, thickly sliced peppers and onion wedges with the chipotle, maple and oil directly on the tray.
Roast twenty-two minutes, turning once at the halfway mark so the tofu browns on more than one face.

recipes.name: Sticky Tempeh Lettuce Cups
steps: Crumble the tempeh into a hot oiled pan and leave it alone for four minutes so one side goes properly crisp.
Pour in the kecap manis and let it bubble down for two minutes until every crumb is lacquered and sticky.
Kill the heat, squeeze in the lime and stir through the sliced chilli.
Spoon into cold lettuce leaves and crush the peanuts over the top.

recipes.name: Tuna and White Bean Smash
steps: Drain the beans and crush about a third of them against the side of the bowl with a fork so the dressing has something to cling to.
Add the tuna with its oil, the finely sliced onion, lemon juice, olive oil and a heavy hand of black pepper.
Fold rather than stir so the tuna stays in flakes, then leave it five minutes and stir the parsley through at the last moment.

recipes.name: Smoked Mackerel and Beetroot Salad
steps: Whisk the yoghurt, horseradish and half the lemon juice into a dressing loose enough to spoon.
Cut the beetroot into wedges and toss with the watercress and the rest of the lemon.
Flake the mackerel over in big pieces, skin discarded, and ripple the horseradish yoghurt through without fully mixing it.

recipes.name: Harissa Prawns with Butter Beans
steps: Soften the sliced garlic in the oil in a wide pan, then stir in the harissa and cook for one minute.
Add the drained butter beans with a splash of water and simmer five minutes, crushing a few against the pan to thicken it.
Lay the prawns on top, cover, and cook three to four minutes until they turn opaque and curl.
Finish with a hard squeeze of lemon straight into the pan.

recipes.name: Nduja Eggs with Greens
steps: Melt the nduja in a cold pan over a low heat until it collapses into a pool of red oil, then add the sliced garlic for thirty seconds.
Pile in the shredded cavolo nero with a splash of water, cover and let it wilt for four minutes.
Make six gaps, crack in the eggs, cover again and cook until the whites just set.
Squeeze the lemon over the greens, not the yolks, and take it to the table in the pan.

recipes.name: Miso Mushroom Pasta
steps: Boil the pasta and keep a mug of the water back when you drain it.
Meanwhile fry the torn mushrooms in a dry hot pan until they squeak and brown, then add the butter and garlic for a minute.
Stir the miso into a few spoons of pasta water and pour it in, scraping the pan, then toss the drained pasta through until the sauce coats it.
Take it off the heat before grating in the parmesan so it melts instead of seizing.

recipes.name: Gochujang Chicken Lettuce Cups
steps: Get a pan very hot, add the sesame oil and the mince, and press it flat so it browns rather than steams.
Break it up after four minutes, stir in the gochujang and cook two more until the paste darkens and clings.
Splash in the vinegar off the heat to cut the sweetness.
Spoon into chilled lettuce leaves with matchsticks of cucumber.

recipes.name: Sumac Halloumi Traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and roast the thickly sliced courgettes, tomatoes and onion wedges in oil for twelve minutes.
Slice the halloumi finger-thick, lay it over the vegetables and dust everything with the sumac.
Roast a further ten minutes until the halloumi is blistered and the tomatoes have burst into the oil.
Tip the pan and spoon the sumac-stained juices back over the cheese.

recipes.name: Ponzu Salmon Bowl
steps: Get the rice on first so it cooks while you deal with everything else.
Sear the salmon skin side down in a dry non-stick pan for five minutes, flip for two, then break it into big flakes in the pan.
Pour the ponzu straight onto the hot pan so it hisses and glazes the fish.
Build the bowls with rice, smashed cucumber, sliced avocado and the salmon, and shower with furikake.

recipes.name: Chilli Oil Silken Tofu
steps: Slide the block of silken tofu out onto a plate in one piece and blot away any water with kitchen paper.
Mix the soy and black vinegar and pour it around the base rather than over the top so the tofu stays white.
Spoon the chilli crisp over the middle and scatter with finely sliced spring onion, then break into it with a spoon at the table.

recipes.name: Preserved Lemon Chicken Traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and scrape the soft pulp from the preserved lemon, keeping the rind to slice into fine strips.
Toss the chicken with the lemon pulp, cumin and oil, then spread it on a tray with the fennel cut into wedges.
Roast twenty-two minutes, adding the olives and lemon rind for the final five so they warm without turning bitter.

recipes.name: Furikake Scrambled Eggs
steps: Beat the eggs with the soy sauce only, no salt, since the furikake will bring its own.
Cook them in a non-stick pan over a low heat, dragging the setting edges into the middle every ten seconds.
Pull the pan off while they still look slightly underdone and let the residual heat finish them.
Slide onto the plate and blanket with furikake and sliced spring onion.

recipes.name: Green Harissa Cod Traybake
steps: Heat the oven to 200C and give the broccoli and tomatoes a ten minute head start on the tray with the oil.
Push them aside, sit the cod in the gap and spread the green harissa thickly over each piece.
Roast a further ten to twelve minutes until the cod is opaque and pushes apart into thick flakes.
Squeeze the lemon over the whole tray while it is still hissing.

recipes.name: Peanut Tofu with Greens
steps: Tear the tofu into chunks and fry in a hot oiled wok, undisturbed, until each face is browned and firm.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy, lime juice and a splash of hot water into a pourable sauce.
Throw the halved pak choi into the wok with a spoon of water, cover for two minutes, then pour in the peanut sauce and toss until it thickens around everything.
Finish with sliced chilli.

recipes.name: Chipotle Black Bean Eggs
steps: Fry the chopped onion until soft and just catching, then stir in the chipotle for a minute.
Add the beans with half their tin liquid and simmer six minutes, mashing a quarter of them so the pan thickens.
Make four wells, crack in the eggs, cover the pan and cook five minutes until the whites set.
Squeeze the lime over and scatter with coriander.

recipes.name: Feta and Pea Frittata
steps: Beat the eggs with plenty of black pepper and only a little salt, since the feta is already salty.
Warm the oil in an ovenproof pan, tip in the frozen peas straight from the bag and let them thaw and sizzle for two minutes.
Pour in the eggs, crumble the feta over and cook on a low heat for six minutes until the edges set.
Slide the pan under a hot grill for three minutes until the top is puffed and golden, then tear the mint over.

recipes.name: Crispy Lentils with Herb Yoghurt
steps: Drain and dry the lentils thoroughly on a tea towel, or they will never crisp.
Fry them in the hot oil in a wide pan, spread out and barely stirred, for eight minutes until they pop and turn nutty, then add the cumin and chilli for the final minute.
Stir the chopped herbs into the yoghurt with a pinch of salt.
Spread the yoghurt on a plate and pile the hot lentils and their spiced oil straight on top.

recipes.name: Smoky Paprika Chickpeas
steps: Fry the sliced garlic gently in the oil, then take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika so it blooms without scorching.
Return to the heat, pour in the passata and the drained chickpeas and simmer eight minutes until the sauce clings.
Sharpen with the sherry vinegar at the very end and check the salt.

recipes.name: Miso Aubergine with Edamame
steps: Heat the oven to 220C, halve the aubergines and score the cut faces in a diamond pattern so the glaze sinks in.
Mix the miso, mirin and vinegar and paint it over the cut sides, then roast cut side up for twenty minutes until collapsing and lacquered.
Scatter the frozen edamame over the tray for the last four minutes to warm through.
Finish with sesame seeds and any glaze left in the tray.

recipes.name: Chilli Crisp Prawns
steps: Bash the cucumber with the flat of a knife, tear it into rough pieces, salt it and leave it to drain while you cook.
Fry the dry prawns in a spoon of the chilli crisp oil over a high heat for ninety seconds a side until just opaque.
Kill the heat, add the chilli crisp solids, soy and lime juice and toss so the prawns are coated.
Tip them over the drained cucumber and scatter with coriander.

recipes.name: Gochujang Cauliflower and Chickpeas
steps: Heat the oven to 220C and whisk the gochujang, maple, vinegar and sesame oil into a loose glaze.
Toss the cauliflower florets and drained chickpeas in half the glaze and spread them out with space between them.
Roast twenty minutes, then brush on the rest of the glaze and give it five more so it sets sticky rather than burns.

recipes.name: Tinned Salmon Cakes
steps: Drain the salmon well, flake it into a bowl and pick out any obvious bones, leaving the soft ones in.
Mix in the egg, mustard, chopped spring onions, lemon zest and half the panko, then shape into six patties and press the rest of the panko onto the outsides.
Shallow fry in a little oil over a medium heat for four minutes a side, turning only once so they hold together.
Serve with the lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.name: Harissa Yoghurt Chicken Salad
steps: Coat the chicken in half the yoghurt with the harissa and a pinch of salt and leave it while the pan gets properly hot.
Cook the thighs in a dry heavy pan for six minutes a side until charred in patches and cooked through, then rest and slice thickly.
Slacken the remaining yoghurt with lemon juice into a dressing.
Toss the lettuce and thick cucumber slices with the dressing and lay the sliced chicken and its pan juices over the top.

recipes.name: Sesame Edamame Smash
steps: Boil the frozen edamame for four minutes, then drain and run cold water over them so they keep their colour.
Crush them roughly with a fork or a couple of pulses in a blender, leaving plenty of texture rather than a puree.
Beat in the tahini, soy, lemon juice and sesame oil, then top with chilli flakes and eat with anything you like.

recipes.name: Za'atar Cauliflower with Tahini
steps: Heat the oven to 230C and toss the cauliflower florets with the oil and half the za'atar, spreading them cut side down.
Roast twenty-two minutes without stirring so the flat faces go deep brown rather than merely soft.
Whisk the tahini with lemon juice and cold water, a spoon at a time, until it seizes and then loosens into a pourable cream.
Pour the tahini over the hot cauliflower and finish with pomegranate and the rest of the za'atar.

recipes.name: Kimchi Tofu Scramble
steps: Squeeze the kimchi dry, chop it, and fry it in the sesame oil for two minutes until the edges caramelise.
Crumble the tofu straight into the pan in uneven pieces and cook five minutes, letting the water cook off before you stir.
Add the turmeric and soy and keep going another three minutes until the curds are golden and dry rather than wet.
Scatter with spring onion off the heat.

recipes.name: Black Garlic Tofu and Green Beans
recipes.hindi: ब्लैक गार्लिक टोफू एंड ग्रीन बीन्स
steps: Mash the black garlic with the soy, vinegar and sesame oil into a dark, almost sweet sauce.
Fry the cubed tofu in a hot wok until three sides are crisp, then lift it out and keep it aside.
Blister the green beans in the same wok over a high heat for four minutes with a splash of water and a lid.
Return the tofu, pour in the black garlic sauce and toss for a minute until everything is glossy.

recipes.name: Tinned Sardine Beans
steps: Tip the oil from the sardine tins into a pan and fry the sliced garlic and chilli flakes in it for a minute.
Add the passata and drained beans and simmer eight minutes until the sauce is thick enough to hold a spoon mark.
Lay the sardines on top and warm them through for two minutes without stirring, so they stay whole.
Shower with parsley and plenty of black pepper.

recipes.name: Sesame Chicken Slaw
steps: Cook the chicken thighs in a dry hot pan, seasoned, for six minutes a side until well browned, then rest and shred with two forks.
Shred the cabbage as finely as you can manage and salt it lightly while the chicken rests.
Whisk the tahini, soy and lime juice with a splash of water into a dressing that pours slowly.
Toss the cabbage, warm chicken and dressing together and crush the peanuts over.

recipes.name: Chorizo and Butter Beans
steps: Fry the sliced chorizo in a cold dry pan so the fat renders out slowly and turns brick red.
Add the sliced onion and cook in that fat for five minutes until soft, then stir in the paprika.
Pour in the passata and the drained butter beans and simmer eight minutes, crushing a few beans to thicken the sauce.
Stir the parsley through at the end and eat straight from the pan.

recipes.name: Creamy Coconut Chickpeas
steps: Fry the sliced garlic in oil for a minute, then stir in the curry powder until it smells toasty.
Tip in the drained chickpeas and the coconut milk and simmer for ten minutes until the sauce thickens.
Stir through the frozen spinach and cook three minutes more until it has wilted down.
Season, squeeze over the lemon and serve.

recipes.name: Smashed Chickpea Sandwich
steps: Drain the chickpeas and crush them roughly with a fork, leaving plenty of texture.
Mix in the tahini, lemon juice, finely chopped onion and celery, then season well.
Pile onto the bread, press the halves together and cut.

recipes.name: Marinated Butter Beans
steps: Drain and rinse the butter beans and tip them into a wide bowl.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice, grated garlic and chilli flakes and season generously.
Pour the dressing over the beans, fold through the chopped parsley and leave ten minutes before eating.

recipes.name: Lemon Butter Bean Mash
steps: Warm the olive oil with the crushed garlic and rosemary until fragrant but not coloured.
Add the drained butter beans with a splash of water and heat through for five minutes.
Crush with a masher to a rough puree, then beat in the lemon zest and juice with plenty of salt.

recipes.name: Green Goddess Beans
steps: Blitz the yoghurt, herbs, garlic, lemon juice and olive oil to a smooth green sauce.
Season the sauce hard — it should taste sharper than you think it needs to.
Fold the drained beans through the sauce and spoon onto a plate with a little more oil on top.

recipes.name: Smoky Black Bean Stew
steps: Soften the chopped onion and garlic in oil for six minutes.
Stir in the smoked paprika and chipotle paste, then the tomatoes, and cook five minutes.
Add the drained black beans and simmer ten minutes, mashing a ladleful against the pan to thicken it.
Season and finish with a squeeze of lime if you have one.

recipes.name: Black Bean Tacos with Lime Slaw
recipes.hindi: ब्लैक बीन टैकोज़ विद लाइम स्लॉ
steps: Shred the cabbage finely and toss it with the juice of one lime and a big pinch of salt.
Fry the drained beans with the cumin in a hot pan for five minutes, crushing about half of them.
Warm the tortillas in the dry pan, then fill with beans, slaw and coriander, with the second lime in wedges.

recipes.name: Charred Courgette with Mint and Chilli
recipes.hindi: चार्ड कोरजेट विद मिंट एंड चिली
steps: Slice the courgettes into thick coins and lay them in a very hot dry pan until charred on both sides.
Move them to a plate and scatter over the sliced chilli, sliced garlic and torn mint while still hot.
Dress with the olive oil and vinegar, season, and leave ten minutes so it all soaks in.

recipes.name: Chickpea Couscous Salad
steps: Pour just-boiled water over the couscous to cover it by a centimetre, cover the bowl and leave five minutes.
Fork the couscous loose, then fold in the drained chickpeas, diced cucumber and chopped parsley.
Dress with the lemon juice and olive oil and season heavily — couscous drinks up salt.

recipes.name: Mustard Lentil Salad
steps: Whisk the mustard, vinegar and olive oil into a thick dressing and season it well.
Stir the finely diced shallot into the dressing and leave five minutes to soften its bite.
Fold through the drained lentils and chopped parsley and eat at room temperature.

recipes.name: Mushroom Lentil Ragu
steps: Chop the mushrooms small and fry them hard in a wide pan until they squeak and brown.
Add the garlic, tomato puree and oregano, cook two minutes, then tip in the tomatoes and drained lentils.
Simmer fifteen minutes while the pasta boils, then toss the drained pasta through with a splash of its water.

recipes.name: Aubergine Chickpea Stew
steps: Cut the aubergine into big chunks and fry in plenty of oil until collapsed and golden, about ten minutes.
Add the garlic and cumin, then the tomatoes and drained chickpeas, and simmer for fifteen minutes.
Stir in the pomegranate molasses, taste for salt and rest it off the heat five minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Smoky Beans on Toast
steps: Fry the sliced garlic with the smoked paprika in oil for one minute.
Add the tomatoes, drained beans and maple syrup and simmer ten minutes until glossy and thick.
Toast the bread, pile the beans on top and finish with a lot of black pepper.

recipes.name: Sticky Sesame Tofu
steps: Press the tofu briefly in a tea towel, cut it into cubes and toss them in the cornflour.
Fry in a non-stick pan over medium heat, turning, until crisp on all sides.
Pour in the soy, maple syrup and vinegar and let it bubble down over the tofu for two minutes until sticky.
Scatter with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

recipes.name: Soy Braised Tofu and Mushrooms
steps: Brown the tofu slabs in a wide pan on both sides, then push them to one side.
Add the sliced mushrooms, ginger, garlic and star anise and fry until the mushrooms give up their water.
Pour in the soy sauce and a cup of water and braise for ten minutes until the liquid turns syrupy.

recipes.name: Maple Soy Tempeh
steps: Slice the tempeh thinly and fry it in oil until deep gold on both sides.
Add the grated garlic and chilli flakes and cook for thirty seconds.
Pour over the soy and maple syrup and shake the pan until every slice is lacquered.
Squeeze the lime over off the heat.

recipes.name: Tofu Larb
steps: Crumble the tofu into a hot dry pan and fry, stirring often, until the pieces are dry and golden at the edges.
Take the pan off the heat and toss the tofu with the lime juice, soy sauce, chilli flakes and finely sliced shallot.
Fold through the torn mint and serve warm with lettuce leaves to scoop it up.

recipes.name: Kimchi Udon with Tofu
steps: Fry the cubed tofu in a wide pan until golden at the edges.
Add the chopped kimchi with its juice and cook two minutes until it smells sweet rather than raw.
Toss in the cooked udon with the soy sauce and a splash of water, then finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

recipes.name: Silken Tofu Chocolate Pots
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bowl set over a pan of just-boiled water, with the heat switched off.
Blitz the silken tofu with the maple syrup and vanilla until completely smooth.
Pour in the melted chocolate, blend again, then divide into glasses and chill until set.

recipes.name: Edamame Pesto Pasta
steps: Boil the pasta, adding the frozen edamame for the last three minutes.
Blitz half the edamame with the basil, almonds, garlic, olive oil and lemon juice into a coarse pesto.
Toss the drained pasta with the pesto, the remaining whole edamame and enough pasta water to make it glossy.

recipes.name: Cold Peanut Noodles
steps: Cook the noodles, adding the edamame for the final two minutes, then rinse both under cold water.
Whisk the peanut butter with the soy, vinegar and four tablespoons of warm water until it loosens into a pourable sauce.
Toss the cold noodles and edamame through the sauce with the shredded cucumber and spoon chilli oil over the top.

recipes.name: Roast Aubergine with Tahini
steps: Halve the aubergines, score the cut sides deeply, oil and salt them and roast cut-side up at 220C for twenty-five minutes.
Loosen the tahini with lemon juice, grated garlic and cold water until it turns pale and pourable.
Spoon the tahini over the hot aubergine and scatter with pomegranate seeds.

recipes.name: Charred Broccoli with Almonds and Chilli
recipes.hindi: चार्ड ब्रोकली विद आमंड्स एंड चिली
steps: Fry the broccoli in a hot pan with a little oil, covered, for six minutes until charred and just tender, then lift it onto a plate.
In the same pan gently fry the sliced almonds, garlic and chilli flakes until the almonds turn gold.
Pour the almond oil over the broccoli and finish with lemon juice and plenty of salt.

recipes.name: Miso Roast Sweet Potato
steps: Cut the sweet potatoes into wedges, toss with oil and roast on a tray at 220C for twenty minutes.
Stir the miso, maple syrup and vinegar together with a splash of water into a loose glaze.
Brush the glaze over the wedges and return them to the oven for five minutes until sticky.
Scatter with sesame seeds and sliced spring onion.

recipes.name: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Traybake
recipes.hindi: स्वीट पोटैटो एंड ब्लैक बीन ट्रेबेक
steps: Cube the sweet potato and toss it on a tray with the wedged onion, cumin, smoked paprika, oil and salt.
Roast at 220C for twenty minutes until the edges catch.
Stir the drained black beans through the tray and roast five minutes more.
Squeeze the lime over everything before serving.

recipes.name: Peanut Sweet Potato Stew
steps: Soften the chopped onion in a deep pan, then add the cubed sweet potato and the chilli flakes.
Tip in the tomatoes and a mug of water and simmer fifteen minutes until the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the peanut butter, drained chickpeas and frozen spinach and cook five minutes more.
Season well — it needs more salt than you expect.

recipes.name: Pea and Mint Soup
steps: Soften the chopped onion in oil in a pot for six minutes without letting it colour.
Add the stock, bring it to the boil and tip in the frozen peas — cook for three minutes only.
Blitz with the mint until smooth and season; the shorter the cooking, the greener it stays.

recipes.name: Broccoli and White Bean Soup
steps: Fry the sliced garlic and chilli flakes in oil in a pot until just golden.
Add the chopped broccoli including the stalk, the drained beans and the stock, and simmer twelve minutes.
Blitz until smooth, loosen with water if it needs it and finish with a hard swirl of olive oil.

recipes.name: Sumac Chickpea Salad
steps: Slice the onion thinly and rub it with the sumac and a pinch of salt until it softens and turns pink.
Toss the drained chickpeas with the chopped tomato, parsley and the sumac onions.
Dress with olive oil and lemon and let it sit five minutes before eating.

recipes.name: Smashed Cucumber Salad
steps: Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife until they split, then tear them into rough chunks.
Salt them in a colander for five minutes and shake off the water that comes out.
Toss with the crushed garlic, soy, vinegar, chilli oil and sesame oil just before eating.

recipes.name: Baked Feta Pasta
steps: Sit the block of feta in the middle of a baking dish, surround it with the tomatoes and garlic and drown everything in olive oil.
Bake at 200C for twenty-five minutes until the tomatoes burst and the feta slumps.
Crush it all together into a sauce with a fork, then fold through the cooked pasta and torn basil.

recipes.name: Cottage Cheese Pasta
steps: Boil the pasta, adding the frozen peas for the last two minutes.
Blitz the cottage cheese with the garlic, lemon zest and a ladle of pasta water until completely smooth.
Off the heat, toss the drained pasta and peas through the sauce with the grated parmesan and a lot of black pepper.

recipes.name: Lentil and Feta Salad
steps: Drain and rinse the lentils and dress them straight away with the oil, vinegar and plenty of salt.
Halve the tomatoes and slice the onion as thinly as you can, then fold both through.
Crumble the feta over the top with the chopped dill and stop mixing there.

recipes.name: Peas and Feta on Toast
steps: Cover the frozen peas with boiling water for two minutes, then drain them well.
Crush the peas roughly with the olive oil, lemon juice, torn mint and half the feta.
Pile onto the toast and crumble the rest of the feta over the top.

recipes.name: Charred Cabbage with Miso Butter
steps: Cut the cabbage into thick wedges through the root so they hold together.
Fry them cut-side down in a hot pan with a little oil until properly blackened, then add a splash of water and cover for eight minutes.
Mash the miso into the soft butter and dot it over the hot cabbage so it melts down between the leaves.
Finish with lemon and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Whipped Feta with Roast Carrots
steps: Halve the carrots lengthways, toss with oil, cumin and salt and roast at 220C for twenty-five minutes.
Blitz the feta with the yoghurt until it is smooth and spoonable.
Spread the whipped feta over a plate, pile the hot carrots on top and trickle over the honey.

recipes.name: Harissa Paneer Traybake
steps: Cube the paneer and cut the peppers and onion into pieces the same size.
Toss everything on a tray with the harissa and oil until it is all coated red.
Roast at 220C for twenty minutes, shaking the tray once, until the edges char.
Squeeze the lemon over the hot tray before serving.

recipes.name: Miso Butter Mushrooms
steps: Fry the halved mushrooms in a dry hot pan until they release their water and it cooks away.
Add the butter and garlic and keep going until the mushrooms are deep brown.
Stir the miso through with a splash of water so it coats everything, then finish with lemon and spring onion.

recipes.name: Miso Butter Corn Ribs
steps: Quarter each cob lengthways into ribs, pressing the knife down slowly through the core.
Toss them with oil and roast on a tray at 220C for twenty minutes until they curl and blister.
Mash the miso into the butter with the gochugaru and brush it over the hot ribs.
Finish with lime juice and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Curried Egg Mayo Sandwich
steps: Boil the eggs for eight minutes, cool them under cold running water and peel.
Mash them roughly with the mayonnaise, curry powder, mango chutney and sliced spring onion.
Season hard and spread it thickly between the bread.
